why: I checked the code, not memory. run_gate passes only NO_CUTOFF=1, and the done recipe's first branch is `[ -z "$(FULL)" ] && verified-done`. For land to reach that branch the stamp must already pass, which means the skill hash has not moved. So for a delta touching only scripts/gates/, land.py or the Makefile, the `done` that GATE_MACHINERY adds can only short-circuit. Since the 415 ruling landed, that rule has never run a gate. All it adds is a line claiming one, and that defect reached main and fired on 430's landing. For l7r/diagram/ci/ the rule is redundant, because the hash moves and the stamp refuses anyway. The GM's 2026-08-25 rule stands: an arbiter's tooling_fix cannot override it, and this one only claimed to. The short-circuit branch already runs hooks-test when the hooks stamp is stale, so the one real gap is tests/tooling. Option (b) would add a new verified-done bypass and a planner path from scripts/ to tests/tooling, inside a feature whose purpose is fewer gate minutes. That is two additions where a narrowing will do. What remains uncovered is the 415 hazard itself: a land.py or gate-script change working beside a real gate is not tested until the next landing that owes a gate anyway. I accept that, because the 415 rule never covered it either. fix_minutes is an estimate of the session's own make test-file FILE=tests/tooling re-run on this firing. The bundle times nothing for it, and 415's 27 minutes belongs to a different cost.

what: Option (a), made before the next tick.
